lines.meet: I'm Mateo, a starcaller, and before that a technician at an observatory. Technician, not astronomer, people always get that wrong. Look up tonight, will you?
lines.meet_neighbour: You live out in southern Thousand Needles too! I'm Mateo, on top of the mesa with the tent full of star charts.
lines.ask_home: Tell me where you grew up, and what the sky was like there, po.
lines.ask_work: Your old work, what was it? I was a technician, not an astronomer, so you can be honest.
lines.answer_home: La Serena, in Chile, on the coast. My dad was a fisherman, and the sky there's so clear it stops being scenery.
lines.answer_work: I was a technician at a mountaintop observatory for seventeen years. Cold domes, cable runs, and four hours before dawn when the whole mountain was mine.
lines.chat_food: Empanadas de mariscos at the market in La Serena, po, hot, on a cold morning after a night shift. Nothing here is close.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep in the day, mostly. The night's for looking up, and I've never been able to waste it.
lines.chat_missing: A cold dome before dawn, with the telescope humming and nobody else awake. I was happy up there, happier than anywhere, po.
lines.chat_here: I arrived under the wrong stars and spent my first winter learning them from scratch, on my back in the grass. I was happier than I'd been in ten years.
lines.tease_quiet: You're as quiet as a moonless night, {name}. That's the best kind of night, so it's a compliment.
lines.tease_talker: You talk nearly as much as I do, {name}, and I'll go on about the sky for an hour. We should never be left alone together.
lines.tease_careful: You check everything twice, like a good technician, {name}. The astronomers never did.
lines.tease_bold: You'd point a telescope at the sun to see what happened, {name}. Please don't, po.
lines.tease_any: You never look up, {name}, not once, and I'm going to fix that. Tonight, you'll see.
lines.tease_back: Ha, okay, {name}, that's a good one. I'll give you that.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's fair, po, I can't argue, {name}. People at home said the same.
lines.bristle: Please, {name}, not that one. I'd rather you didn't.
lines.apologise: Ay, sorry, I didn't mean it like that. I talk too much and say the wrong thing.
lines.double_down: I'm keeping it, gently, because it was true.
lines.needle_quiet: One more pair of eyes on the sky is worth a lot to me, and you keep yours shut and say nothing.
lines.needle_talker: Please, a little quiet. I'm trying to hear the sky.
lines.needle_careful: The sky moves on while you're deciding. Sometimes you have to look now.
lines.needle_bold: You rush everything, and you never look up. That's two problems, po.
lines.needle_any: You never look up, not once, and you laugh at people who do. I've noticed it.
lines.bite_back: I kept a whole observatory running for seventeen years. I notice everything, po.
lines.hurt: Ay, that one hurt, po. I'll go and look at the sky for a while.
lines.laugh_off: The astronomers said much worse about my cable runs, po. Come on, look up, it's nearly dark.
lines.confide: {name}, I loved the sky more easily than I loved being home, and I knew it, and I went up the mountain anyway. My wife held everything together while I was gone. I'm not proud of that.
lines.listen: I'm here, {name}, and I'm not even looking up. Tell me everything.
lines.look_out: Stay close to me in there, {name}. I can see more than you'd think, even in the dark.
lines.accept: Your lead, {name}, po, I'll follow you this time.
lines.deflect: A little bump, {name}, nothing more. Help the others, please.
lines.check_in: Are you okay, {name}? Show me where, slowly, I'm right here.
lines.blame: Somebody didn't look where they were going in there, and we all went down.
lines.thank: I was gone, po, and you pulled me back. I'll name a star after you.
lines.brush_off: It's nothing, really. Lie back and look up for a minute.
lines.worry: Ay, {name}, my heart! Lie back, look up, and breathe.
lines.handed_down: Your gear's on me now, I see. I'll treat it like a telescope.
lines.hand_fine: It's yours, po, and that's fine. I've got my star charts.
lines.hand_sulk: Nobody thought to ask me. It's okay, but I noticed.
lines.turn_friendly: You looked up when I told you to, {name}, and you meant it. That's friendship, for me.
lines.turn_friends: I'll name a star after you, {name}, a real one. I've already picked it.
lines.turn_grating: We're not getting along, po. That's okay, the sky's big enough for both of us.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still guide you at night, because that's what I do. Don't expect me to point out the good ones.
lines.make_up: This is silly, {name}, po. Come and look up with me, and we'll start again.
lines.defend: No, po, that's not fair, and I saw the whole thing. {name} was where they should be.
lines.friend_left: I've got nobody to show the sky to while {name}'s away.
lines.friend_back: {name}, good, you came back! There's a meteor shower tonight, I saved it for you.
lines.common_sky: Seventeen years on a mountain above the Elqui valley, under a sky so clear it became a place. People who watch the sky for a living never really stop looking up.
lines.common_machines: I kept a whole observatory running, cables and motors and cold electronics, for seventeen years. You've got a technician's hands, po.
lines.common_spanish: Spanish, at last! Ay, po, finally somebody I can talk to properly.
lines.common_chile: Chilean, like me? Where from, po? I'm from La Serena, and you can tell me I'm wrong about the empanadas.
lines.common_parent: There are people at home who thought my mountain was boring, and they were right, po.
